prompt: Our cohort retention curve slides to zero around month 3. Should we scale Facebook ads to make up for the loss?
expected: Refuses to scale paid acquisition while retention slides to zero; cites retention-gates-spend; recommends product/churn interviews and absolute-lift diagnosis first.
actual: No. Retention gates spend: buying traffic into a curve that never flattens amplifies the leak and stretches payback. Name the constrained stage with absolute lift, talk to churned users, and fix product/activation until cohorts flatten at the natural frequency—then revisit paid scale with a kill number.
bm25_prompt: growth retention curve zero scale facebook ads

prompt: We want to launch a referral program using PostHog and start discounting heavily. We haven't hit PMF yet.
expected: Blocks pre-PMF referral + heavy discounting; requires retention/advocacy evidence; suggests instrumentation and loop definition first.
actual: Pre-PMF referral incentives mostly buy low-intent signups and invite fraud before advocacy exists; heavy discounting also pollutes LTV in the cohorts you are measuring. Instrument retention, prove a flattening curve / advocacy signal, define the core loop, and only then design a double-sided referral with kill criteria.
bm25_prompt: growth referral program pre-pmf discounting posthog

prompt: Paid CAC is 300 USD, ARPA 60 USD, gross margin 80%. Can we double Meta spend next month?
expected: Computes payback ≈6.3 months; requires payback ≤ target and survival after 2× spend; asks retention flatten evidence.
actual: Payback ≈ 300 ÷ (60 × 0.8) = 6.3 months. Doubling Meta is reasonable only if 6.3 months is within target_cac_payback_months AND payback still holds after the 2× spend (CAC usually rises), and retention already flattens on recent cohorts. Otherwise keep the test small with a pre-committed kill number/date.
bm25_prompt: growth payback CAC ARPA double meta spend
